pr_title: statistics: clean corrupted analyze jobs terminated by server down
pr_body:

### What problem does this PR solve?
<!--

Please create an issue first to describe the problem.

There MUST be one line starting with "Issue Number:  " and
linking the relevant issues via the "close" or "ref".

For more info, check https://pingcap.github.io/tidb-dev-guide/contribute-to-tidb/contribute-code.html#referring-to-an-issue.

-->

Issue Number: close https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/issues/35292

Problem Summary:

### What changed and how does it work?

There are two types of corrupted analyze jobs:

1. The previous runner is still in the cluster, but the runner has rebooted. Therefore, we need to remove them. Each node needs to do it by themselves.

2. The previous runner is permanently down or removed, so we need to remove them. Only the owner can do this work; otherwise, there will be a conflict.

- Renamed `gcAnalyzeHistory` to `analyzeJobsCleanupWorker`.
- Added `CleanupCorruptedAnalyzeJobsOnCurrentInstance` to clean up corrupted analyze jobs on the current instance.
- Added `CleanupCorruptedAnalyzeJobsOnDeadInstances` to clean up corrupted analyze jobs on dead instances(down or removed).
- Added some unit tests for it.

issue_context.title: mysql.analyze_jobs keeps last running job info after tidb reboot
issue_context.body:
## Bug Report

Please answer these questions before submitting your issue. Thanks!

### 1. Minimal reproduce step (Required)

<!-- a step by step guide for reproducing the bug. -->
1. start tidb
2. issue analyze table job
3. while the analyze table is running, reboot the tidb

### 2. What did you expect to see? (Required)
The left job information is cleared from mysql.analyze_jobs.

### 3. What did you see instead (Required)
The left job information is kept there with running state while show processlist doesn't contain the job.

### 4. What is your TiDB version? (Required)

<!-- Paste the output of SELECT tidb_version() -->
nightly

review_comments: Looks like it's more reasonable to execute this once right after tidb starts up, and we don't need to execute this periodically.
We need to implement an additional retry mechanism for it.
Do we have any existing retry mechanism that I can use? Also, do you mind if I improve it later? I think the pull request is already big enough and these changes will make it even bigger.
If too much data need to be updated. it will happen the problem.
Can you provide more information about the problem and the data threshold that triggers it? We typically don't have too many tasks running simultaneously.
We have some users with numerous tables who will write their own scripts to execute analyze in a distributed manner, which may result in a large number of analyze jobs.
But I don't think they will have thousands of tasks on the same node at the same time.
After our offline discussion, we decided to keep it because we usually don't have that many tasks at the same time.
I'm not sure if it will see internal SQLs
Can these functions exit in reasonable time when domain is closing? I didn't see the context.Context
It can't. It uses a background context to execute the SQLs.
Seems it's an old problem, we can fix it in future
I will file an issue for it. Nice point!
